name: table
title: Table
description: Rows of records with sortable columns, selection and sideways scroll.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called with the new sort; rows are sorted by value unless `manualSort` is set.

props.name: manualSort
props.description: Leave rows in the order given (sort them yourself in onSortChange).

props.name: rowLabel
props.description: Names a row for its select checkbox ("Select Acme Corp" instead of "Select row 3"), e.g. `(row) => row.name`. `index` is the row's place as shown, from 0. Without it the checkbox says the row's number, which changes when the table is sorted.

props.name: renderCell
props.type: (cell: { row: R; column: Column<R>; index: number; content: React.ReactNode }) => React.ReactNode
props.description: Draws every body cell's content, after the column's own `cell`: `content` is what the cell would show. Wrap it (a link to the row's page), or replace it; the cell keeps its padding, alignment and truncation.

props.name: renderRow
props.type: (row: { row: R; index: number; selected: boolean; rowProps: React.ComponentProps<'tr'>; children: React.ReactNode }) => React.ReactNode
props.description: Draws each body row. Spread `rowProps` (state and styles) on your `<tr>` and put `children` (the cells) inside, to add a handler, a data attribute or a context provider: `renderRow={({ row, rowProps, children }) => <tr {...rowProps} onClick={() => open(row)}>{children}</tr>}`.
